proposals.before: In the fourth month Minister of Education Lu Fafa surrendered Yingzhou to Qi; Jiangzhou inspector Hou Tian was sent against him.
proposals.after: In the fourth month Minister of Education Lu Fahe surrendered Yingzhou to Qi; Jiangzhou inspector Hou Tian was sent against him.
proposals.reason: 陸法和 is Lu Fahe, not Lu Fafa.

proposals.before: In the fourth month, Minister of Education Lu Fafa attached Yingzhou to Qi; they sent Jiangzhou Inspector Hou Tian to suppress him.
proposals.after: In the fourth month, Minister of Education Lu Fahe attached Yingzhou to Qi; they sent Jiangzhou Inspector Hou Tian to suppress him.
proposals.reason: 陸法和 should be romanized Lu Fahe.

proposals.before: On wuwu his birth mother, Consort Xia Gui, was honored as empress dowager.
proposals.after: On wuwu his birth mother, Worthy Consort Xia, was honored as empress dowager.
proposals.reason: 夏貴妃 is Worthy Consort Xia; 貴妃 is the title, not a given name Gui.

proposals.before: On wuwu his birth mother Consort Xia Gui was honored as empress dowager.
proposals.after: On wuwu his birth mother Worthy Consort Xia was honored as empress dowager.
proposals.reason: 貴妃 is a consort rank title, not part of the personal name.

proposals.before: Hou, son of former Yong'an marquis Que, succeeded as Prince of Shaoling to serve Empress Hou.
proposals.after: Hou, son of former Yong'an marquis Que, succeeded as Prince of Shaoling to attend upon the consort of Prince Xie.
proposals.reason: 攜王后 is the consort of Prince Xie (攜王), not 'Empress Hou'.

proposals.before: The former Marquis of Yong'an Que's son Hou succeeded to enfeoffment as Prince of Shaoling, attending upon Empress Hou of Emperor Xie.
proposals.after: The former Marquis of Yong'an Que's son Hou succeeded to enfeoffment as Prince of Shaoling, attending upon the consort of Prince Xie.
proposals.reason: 攜王后 means the consort of Prince Xie, not Empress Hou of Emperor Xie.

proposals.after: East Yangzhou inspector Zhang Biao besieged Linhai administrator Wang Huaizhen at Yan Rock.
proposals.reason: 臨海 is Linhai, not Taizhou.

proposals.before: East Yangzhou Inspector Zhang Biao besieged Taizhou Administrator Wang Huaizhen at Yan Rock.
proposals.after: East Yangzhou Inspector Zhang Biao besieged Linhai Administrator Wang Huaizhen at Yan Rock.

proposals.before: Central Guard General Prince Dakuen of Linchuan received a gate equal to the Three Excellencies at his existing rank; Central Protector Prince Dacheng of Guiyang became Protector-General of the Army.
proposals.after: Central Guard General Prince Dakuan of Linchuan received a gate equal to the Three Excellencies at his existing rank; Central Protector Prince Dacheng of Guiyang became Protector-General of the Army.
proposals.reason: 大款 is Dakuan, not Dakuen.

proposals.before: On jiawu former Shouchang magistrate Liu Rui was made Prince of Yiyin; former Pacify West legal bureau acting staff officer Xiao Hong was made Prince of Baling to attend the Song and Qi empresses.
proposals.after: On jiawu former Shouchang magistrate Liu Rui was made Prince of Ruyin; former Pacify West legal bureau acting staff officer Xiao Dan was made Prince of Baling to attend the Song and Qi empresses.
proposals.reason: 汝陰 is Ruyin, not Yiyin; 蕭紞 is Xiao Dan (packet 'Hong' is a slip).

proposals.before: On jiawu former Shouchang magistrate Liu Rui was made Prince of Yiyin; former Pacify West legal bureau acting staff officer Xiao Hong was made Prince of Baling, attending upon the empresses of Song and Qi.
proposals.after: On jiawu former Shouchang magistrate Liu Rui was made Prince of Ruyin; former Pacify West legal bureau acting staff officer Xiao Dan was made Prince of Baling, attending upon the empresses of Song and Qi.

proposals.before: Grand Mentor and Guangzhou inspector Xiao Bo rebelled; he sent Ouyang He, Fu Tai, and his nephew Zi as the vanguard; South Jiangzhou inspector Yu Xiaoping joined him with troops.
proposals.after: Grand Mentor and Guangzhou inspector Xiao Bo rebelled; he sent Ouyang He, Fu Tai, and his nephew Zi as the vanguard; South Jiangzhou inspector Yu Xiaoqing joined him with troops.
proposals.reason: 余孝頃 is Yu Xiaoqing, not Yu Xiaoping.

proposals.before: Grand Mentor and Guangzhou Inspector Xiao Bo raised troops in revolt; he sent false commander Ouyang He, Fu Tai, and Bo's nephew son Zi as forward army; South Jiangzhou Inspector Yu Xiaoping joined with troops.
proposals.after: Grand Mentor and Guangzhou Inspector Xiao Bo raised troops in revolt; he sent false commander Ouyang He, Fu Tai, and Bo's nephew Zi as forward army; South Jiangzhou Inspector Yu Xiaoqing joined with troops.
proposals.reason: 余孝頃 should be Yu Xiaoqing throughout.

proposals.after: Xiao Zi and Yu Xiaoqing's armies withdrew and fled.
proposals.reason: Consistent correction of 余孝頃 to Yu Xiaoqing.

proposals.after: Xiao Zi and Yu Xiaoqing's armies retreated and fled.
proposals.reason: Consistent correction of 余孝頃 to Yu Xiaoqing.

proposals.before: On wuxu Hou Andu advanced; Yu Xiaoxiang fled; Xiao Zi surrendered, and Yuzhang was pacified.
proposals.after: On wuxu Hou Andu advanced; Yu Xiaoqing fled; Xiao Zi surrendered, and Yuzhang was pacified.
proposals.reason: 余孝頃 was earlier Xiaoping and here Xiaoxiang; both should be Xiaoqing.

proposals.after: On wuxu, Hou Andu advanced his army; Yu Xiaoqing abandoned his force and fled; Xiao Zi asked to surrender, and Yuzhang was pacified.
proposals.reason: Unify 余孝頃 as Yu Xiaoqing.

proposals.after: On wuchen Yu Xiaoqing sent envoys to the chancellor's office to surrender.
proposals.reason: Unify 余孝頃 as Yu Xiaoqing.

proposals.after: On wuchen, Yu Xiaoqing sent envoys to the Chancellor's office begging to surrender.

proposals.before: The historical minister, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke of Zheng Wei Zheng, said, "The High Ancestor was indeed one whom Heaven let range freely: intelligent and versed in antiquity, his Way nearly matched innate knowledge; his learning made him broadly informed, truly civil and martial, accomplished in many arts and talents.
proposals.after: The historiographer, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke of Zheng Wei Zheng, said, "The High Ancestor was indeed one whom Heaven let range freely: intelligent and versed in antiquity, his Way nearly matched innate knowledge; his learning made him broadly informed, truly civil and martial, accomplished in many arts and talents.
proposals.reason: 史臣 is the standard historiographer's voice formula; 'historical minister' mistranslates the office/role and obscures that this is the historian's appraisal.

proposals.before: He said Zhou could be punished; allies assembled unlooked-for; he leapt like a dragon at Fan and Han and struck like lightning at Xiang and Ying; cutting Li was like shaking dry stalks; taking the lone tyrant was like picking up what was lost.
proposals.after: He said Zhou could be punished; allies assembled unlooked-for; he leapt like a dragon at Fan and Han and struck like lightning at Xiang and Ying; cutting down those of alienated virtue was like shaking dry stalks; taking the lone tyrant was like picking up what was lost.
proposals.reason: 剪離德 means cutting down the alienated-in-virtue (the disloyal), not a person named Li; the idiomatic rendering invents a false personal name.

proposals.before: Emperor Jing met with an unpropitious house and inherited this time of hardship; campaigns issued from elsewhere and government and punishment were not in his own hands; at the time there were no Yi and Huo to assist him—how could he not yield the throne high?"
proposals.after: Emperor Jing encountered disaster in his ruling house and inherited these troubled times. Military campaigns were directed by others, and neither government nor punishment lay in his own hands. With no Yi Yin or Huo Guang to support him, how could he have avoided the lofty act of yielding the throne?"
proposals.reason: The draft’s ‘yield the throne high’ is ungrammatical. 高讓 means a lofty or noble act of yielding, and 伊、霍 are the historical exemplars Yi Yin and Huo Guang.

proposals.before: Emperor Jing met an unpropitious house and inherited hardship; campaigns issued elsewhere and government and punishment were not his own; with no Yi and Huo to assist, how could he not yield the throne high?"
proposals.after: Emperor Jing inherited a dynasty in ruin and an age of upheaval. Armies marched at another’s command, and neither government nor justice was his to direct. With no Yi Yin or Huo Guang to support him, how could he have avoided yielding the throne?"
proposals.reason: The draft is ungrammatical and leaves the paired allusion opaque. 高讓 refers to yielding the throne, while 伊、霍 are Yi Yin and Huo Guang, exemplary regents invoked as the support Emperor Jing lacked.

decisions.reason: s0004 names 陸法和; 法和 is Fahe, so Lu Fafa is a romanization error and Lu Fahe is the correct replacement.
The same unit’s 陸法和 must be romanized Lu Fahe in the literal field; Fafa misreads 和.
s0022’s 夏貴妃 is surname Xia plus the consort rank 貴妃 (Worthy Consort), not a given name Gui; Worthy Consort Xia matches the title formula.
Literal likewise mistook 貴妃 for a personal name; replacing Consort Xia Gui with Worthy Consort Xia restores the rank title.
s0038 ends 奉攜王后: 攜王 is Prince Xie and 后 his consort, not an Empress Hou; the repair correctly has him attend that consort.
Literal’s Empress Hou of Emperor Xie invents an empress and misreads 攜王; consort of Prince Xie is the source-supported reading.
s0041 has 臨海太守; 臨海 is Linhai, not the modern/anachronistic Taizhou.
The literal field repeats Taizhou for 臨海; Linhai Administrator is the accurate place-title pairing.
s0044’s 大款 is Dakuan; Dakuen is a misromanization of 款.
s0072 has 汝陰王 and 蕭紞: 汝陰 is Ruyin (not Yiyin), and 紞 is Dan (not Hong); both proposed name fixes match the Chinese.
Literal carries the same two errors; Ruyin and Xiao Dan are required by 汝陰 and 蕭紞.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 劉叡爲汝陰王……蕭紞爲巴陵王

decisions.reason: s0093’s 余孝頃 is Yu Xiaoqing; Xiaoping misreads 頃.
Literal must likewise use Yu Xiaoqing for 余孝頃; dropping the calque ‘nephew son’ for 從子 as nephew leaves sense intact.
s0098 again names 余孝頃; consistent Yu Xiaoqing replaces the earlier Xiaoping error.
Literal of s0098 needs the same Yu Xiaoqing correction for 余孝頃.
s0109’s 余孝頃 was wrongly rendered Xiaoxiang; unifying to Yu Xiaoqing matches the Chinese name.
Literal likewise requires Yu Xiaoqing for 余孝頃 in this unit.
s0112’s subject is still 余孝頃; Yu Xiaoqing is the correct romanization in place of Xiaoxiang.
Literal of s0112 must use Yu Xiaoqing for the same 余孝頃.

decisions.reason: s0139 opens 史臣侍中; 史臣 is the historiographer’s voice (as in adjacent 史臣曰), not ‘historical minister’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 史臣侍中、鄭國公魏徵曰

decisions.reason: 剪離德 is ‘cut down those of alienated virtue,’ not a person Li; the proposed idiomatic removes the invented name and restores the parallel with 取獨夫.

The Chinese predicates external control over military, government, and punishment before asking how Emperor Jing could avoid 高讓. The proposal restores grammatical English and correctly expands the conventional Yi Yin and Huo Guang pairing.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時無伊、霍之輔，焉得不爲高讓歟

decisions.reason: The idiomatic revision accurately renders the loss of independent command and government, identifies the paired regent allusion, and expresses 高讓 as yielding the throne rather than the nonsensical phrase 'yield the throne high.'

sourceWitness.excerpt: 征伐有所自出，政刑不由於己

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0010 shows English Xiao Hong came only from the bad reading of 蕭紞; the personal-name claim’s en value must read Xiao Dan.
